stem: Nitrogen molecules, $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$, contain two atoms attracted to each other by a triple covalent bond.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe how the triple covalent bond forms in a $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ molecule. Refer to orbital overlap and hybridisation in your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Nitrogen oxides, $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{NO}$, are produced in internal combustion engines. Release of these gases into the atmosphere leads to the formation of photochemical smog.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Outline how nitrogen oxides are involved in the formation of photochemical smog.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Construct an equation to demonstrate how a catalytic converter reduces the amount of nitrogen oxide gases released into the atmosphere.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
$\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ is very unreactive. It is difficult to make ammonia, $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, directly from its elements but it can be made from $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl(s)}$.

Identify a reagent and the conditions required to make $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$ from $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl(s)}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
$25\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCl(aq)}$ is added to a beaker and its pH is recorded.

$50\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ is added to the $\text{HCl(aq)}$ in $5\text{ cm}^3$ portions.

The pH of the mixture is monitored until all the $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ is added.

$\text{HCl}$ is a strong Brønsted-Lowry acid.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Describe what is meant by a strong Brønsted-Lowry acid.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{NH}_3$ is a weak base.

Construct an equation that shows the behaviour of $\text{NH}_3$ as a weak Brønsted-Lowry base when dissolved in water.
